title: Azure Local infrastructure.yml (cicd_infra)
description: The part of infrastructure.yml that the tool 'cicd_infra' reads. Generated from master-registry.yaml; every key is also in the full schema.

schema_version.description: The schema version this file follows. Major 5. A minor version adds optional keys only; a major version can rename or remove keys. Each key's description says which version added it ('since'). Version history, in order: 5.2 adds nodes[].network_adapters, BIOS settings, the site IP range and the maintenance environment's network. 5.3 adds the BIOS phases (bios_during_provisioning), networking.management.static_method and provisioning_dhcp_range, nodes[].maintenance_address, provisioning.simplified.maintenance_password, and the SAN details (storage.san.array, fibre_channel and iscsi, nodes[].san); it also adds _metadata.scope: ztp for a file that holds only what azurelocal-ztp reads. 5.4 puts every azurelocal-ztp setting in this schema, so no tool keeps a key of its own: the BIOS actions ZTP derives from the hardware inventory (provisioning.simplified.isolate_san_adapters and enable_embedded_nics, nodes[].san.hbas[].type), the Azure resource choices, timeouts, retries, the USB image and the maintenance environment of simplified provisioning, and hardware.bmc.rfs_write_attribute and verify_certificate. 5.4.1 adds provisioning.simplified.timeouts.adapters_minutes. 5.4.2 adds hardware.sbe.delivery and node_pull_url (how the SBE package reaches the nodes during OS configuration). 5.4.3 adds os_configuration.clear_storage, the switch that lets the OS configuration run wipe leftover local storage. 5.4.4 adds os_configuration.network (confirm_minutes, stable_seconds: the commit-confirmed window of a guarded network change) and os_configuration.remoting with transport, bootstrap_transport and allowed_source_cidrs. 5.5 puts the CI/CD infrastructure in devops (the project, its settings, the environments, the Azure sign-in, the runners with their network and roles) and adds the domain join (identity.active_directory.domain_join_account, join_options, local_admin_members). 5.6 adds the deployment block (the timeouts, polling, approval and resume of the toolkit's Validate and Deploy run) and the remote management security profile: scenario.environment_class, the profile keys of os_configuration.remoting (allow_any_source, trusted_hosts, use_https, isolation_confirmed, certificate; bootstrap_transport also takes smb and auto) and a purpose marker on networking.logical_networks[] and networking.cluster_networks[] (the values management and oob of networking.vlans[].purpose also count). A missing scenario.environment_class means production. 5.6.1 adds identity.active_directory.security_groups[].local_groups. 5.6.2 identifies the adapters of nodes[].network_adapters[] by hardware facts (mac_address is required; port_index, pci_location, vendor, os_name_override and allowed_vlans are optional). 5.6.3 adds enabled, ip_allocation_method and nsg_name to networking.logical_networks[]. A file written for 5.6.0 stays valid: a minor version adds optional keys only, except that 5.6.2 requires the MAC of every adapter. 5.6.4 adds the SBE package as a requirement: hardware.sbe.requirement and not_applicable_reason (whether the OEM package is required, or not applicable with a reason), source_path (the share or folder where the downloaded package is available to the automation), source_username and source_password (the read credential, a Key Vault reference), and the optional package_sha256 and package_size_bytes. The build-time side-load (delivery) is unchanged and stays off by default. 5.6.5 adds landing_zone.policy (required_tags, management_group): the tag names and the management group of the Tier 1 tag policy, which the Azure Policy task assigns in audit mode. 5.6.6 adds operations.monitoring.action_group: the name of the Azure Monitor action group that the alerting task creates. 5.6.7 adds security.defender_for_cloud: the free level of Microsoft Defender for Cloud that Azure Local needs. 5.6.8 adds security.defender_for_cloud.security_contact_email. 5.6.9 adds the storage keys the volume and storage path scripts read: storage.pool, storage.csv, storage.paths and, on storage.volumes, provisioning_type, file_system, parity_percent, media_type and deduplication. 5.6.10 adds what the SAN deployment needs: networking.cluster_network_properties and, for iSCSI, storage.san.iscsi.networks, jumbo_packet and chap.mutual. 5.6.11 adds what the logical network, network security group and VM image scripts read: networking.network_security_groups (name and rules with name, priority, direction, access, protocol, source and destination address prefixes and port ranges, description), networking.logical_networks[].vm_switch_name and storage.vm_images (name, os_type, publisher, offer, sku, version, storage_path). 5.6.12 adds operations.monitoring.retention_days and removes operations.notifications.teams_webhook and operations.monitoring.health_alerts. 5.6.13 adds the secrets section (provider, file directory, command) and lets a secret reference use the env://, file:// and command:// forms besides keyvault://. 5.6.14 adds hardware.inventory (output_directory, file_name_prefix, format, timeout_seconds), which Get-HardwareInventory.ps1 reads. 5.6.15 adds what Enable-ArcSdn.ps1 reads: sdn.acknowledge_maintenance_window and sdn.acknowledge_dns_record, the rules of sdn.prefix, and sdn.dns_records (read now); it removes sdn.default_access_policy. 5.6.16 adds storage.san.luns[].unique_id (how New-SanVolume.ps1 finds the disk of a LUN) and removes security.backup_key_vault. 5.6.17 adds landing_zone.management_groups[].role and azure.automation_identity.object_id (the two keys the Terraform landing zone and identity modules need) and makes the Terraform and Ansible code readers of the file (New-IacVariableFiles.ps1). 5.6.19 adds provisioning.iso.image_uri (the address Invoke-MountGoldImageISO.ps1 gives the BMC virtual media), landing_zone.subscriptions[].billing_scope and workload, point_to_site.protocols, root_certificate_name and root_certificate, bastion.network and the nat_gateway object of landing_zone.connectivity, and a list of values for landing_zone.virtual_machines[].os. 5.6.20 adds operations.updates.install_after_deployment and operations.updates.target_version (read by Start-SolutionUpdateAfterDeployment.ps1) and removes keys that no tool read (see MIGRATION, To 5.6.20). 5.6.21 adds landing_zone.network_security_groups[] (the network security groups of the Azure landing zone networks: name and rules, created by New-LandingZoneNsg.ps1) and security.baseline_settings[] (type, name, value and acknowledge_weaker_security of the security baseline settings that Set-SecurityBaselines.ps1 changes with Set-AzsSecurity). 5.6.23 adds landing_zone.networks[].allow_forwarded_traffic, allow_gateway_transit and use_remote_gateways (the options of the virtual network peerings Deploy-VirtualNetworks.ps1 makes) and identity.active_directory.precreate_computer_objects (Set-ADConfiguration.ps1 pre-creates the computer objects of the machines and the cluster). 5.6.24 adds hardware.sbe.partner_properties[] (name and value pairs that the hardware vendor's SBE asks for; ARM partnerProperties) and hardware.sbe.partner_credentials[] (secret_name and secret: the secret that the SBE needs, which the deployment template writes into the cluster Key Vault under secret_name; secret is a reference, never the value; ARM partnerCredentiallist). 5.6.25 adds devops.pipelines.runner_label and devops.pipelines.environments.* (the runner label and the approval environment of each of the toolkit's pipelines; task 05 sets them as pipeline variables). 5.6.26 removes registry entries that only the old variables.yml layout had (environment.env_name, env_type, env_owner and env_description, site.env_name and identity.active_directory.security_groups_by_role); a file never accepted them, so a file of any 5.6 version stays valid. 5.6.27 adds devops.pipelines.service_connection and devops.pipelines.variable_group (Azure DevOps: the names of the service connection and the variable group task 05 creates and the pipelines take as run parameters); a file without them stays valid. 5.6.28 adds the keys every pipeline, Ansible role, Terraform module and config template reads instead of a value of its own (devops.pipelines.infrastructure_file, handoff_path and tool_versions, devops.state.*, devops.runners[].*, devops.runner_network.*, devops.runner_access, identity.active_directory functional levels and DNS forwarders, landing_zone connectivity, virtual machine, policy and key vault keys, security.defender_for_cloud alert keys, network_devices[] ports, MTU and HA, hardware.sbe.requirement vendor); every key is optional, so a file of any 5.6 version stays valid. 5.6.29 adds deployment.events_directory (the one folder where the toolkit runs write their event feeds and Sonar reads them); a file without it stays valid. 5.6.30 adds landing_zone.budgets[] (the Cost Management budgets that Deploy-CostBudgets.ps1 creates: name, scope, subscription, resource_group, amount, time_grain, start_date, end_date, thresholds, forecast_thresholds, contact_emails); a file without it stays valid. 5.6.31 adds operations.monitoring.action_group_enable_if_disabled (whether the alerting task enables an action group that exists but is disabled; default false, report only); a file without it stays valid. The current version is 5.6.31.

scope.description: Schema 5.3. full (default): the whole instance, so every design section is required (scenario, environment, cluster, networking.intents, identity and the sections a scenario choice makes required). ztp: a file for azurelocal-ztp on its own, with no automation after it. It holds only what ZTP reads, so the cluster deployment's sections (cluster, intents, storage, identity) are not required. Use infrastructure.ztp.example.yml to start one. To grow it into the full file, add the rest and set scope to full (or remove the key). From 5.6.33 two more kinds of scope exist. A planning scope (trailwright, surveyor) marks a whole design written by a planning tool: everything full requires is required, except the MACs of the ports (nodes[].network_adapters[].mac_address, nodes[].management.mac_address), which hardware discovery fills; set scope to full once discovery has run. A tool scope (os_configuration, deployment, cicd_infra, terraform, ansible, monitoring, discovery, ranger, beacon, s2d_cartographer, loadtools, draftsman) marks a cut that New-InfrastructureArtifacts.ps1 -Cut <tool> wrote: it holds only the keys that tool reads, and Test-InfrastructureFile.ps1 (Test-AzlInfrastructure, Import-AzlInfrastructure) checks it against schema/tools/<tool>.schema.json instead of the full schema. Every tool of _tool_catalog that has keys is a value here (the generator stops when one is missing).

file_version.description: Your own version of this file.

last_updated.description: Date of the last change, YYYY-MM-DD.

generated_by.description: The tool that wrote the file, for example azurelocal-trailwright 1.1.0. Empty when written by hand.

notes.description: Free text about this file for the people who keep it. Not read by the tools.

tags.description: Azure tags applied to the resources the tools create. A policy that requires tags isn't supported by simplified provisioning.

azure.description: The Azure targets of the instance: tenant, region, and the subscription and resource group of the Arc machines, the cluster and (unless provisioning.simplified says otherwise) the site and edge machines.

tenant_id.description: Microsoft Entra tenant ID (GUID) of the subscription. Read it with (Get-AzContext).Tenant.Id or from the Microsoft Entra ID overview page in the Azure portal.

location.description: Azure region, for example eastus. Simplified provisioning works only in eastus in the preview.

subscription_id.description: Subscription ID (GUID) of the Arc machines and the cluster, and of the site and edge machines unless provisioning.simplified.subscription_id names another one. Read it with (Get-AzContext).Subscription.Id.

resource_group.description: Resource group of the Arc machines and the cluster: 1 to 90 characters (letters, digits, hyphen, underscore, period, parentheses). The Azure Local resource provider needs the Azure Connected Machine Resource Manager role on it; the ZTP template assigns that role.

automation_identity.description: The identity that runs automation with no one signed in (pipelines, ZTP, the ARM deployment).

type.description: The kind of identity that runs the automation: a managed identity (preferred, no secret to keep) or a service principal.

name.description: Managed identity resource name, or the service principal's display name.

client_id.description: Client (application) ID of the identity (GUID). Not a secret.

resource_group.description: Resource group that holds the identity.

key_vaults.description: Every Key Vault that a keyvault:// reference in this file names, with where it is. Tools resolve references against this list, and grant roles on the vault from it.

name.description: Key Vault name, as a keyvault://<name>/<secret> reference uses it: 3 to 24 characters, letters, digits and hyphens.

resource_group.description: Resource group that holds the vault.

purpose.description: What the vault holds, for example management, deployment or backup.

secrets.description: Schema 5.6.13. Where the toolkit reads secrets from. Every secret in this file is a reference, never a value; a reference names its own provider in its scheme: keyvault://<vault>/<secret> (Azure Key Vault, the default), env://<VARIABLE_NAME>, file://<name> or command://<name>. One file can mix providers. A file or command reference holds a NAME only: the directory of the secret files and the command are set here, so a reference in a shared file cannot point a machine at an arbitrary path or run an arbitrary command. Optional; every key has a default. See docs/secret-references.md.

provider.description: Schema 5.6.13. The provider New-AzlSecretReference uses for a new reference when the caller does not name one. It does not change how an existing reference is read: that follows the reference's own scheme. Default keyvault.

file.description: Schema 5.6.13. Settings of the file provider (file://<name>). Needed only when a reference uses it.

directory.description: Schema 5.6.13. The absolute path of the directory that holds the secret files. file://<name> reads the file <name> in it: one secret per file, UTF-8, the trailing line break removed. A name cannot hold a path, so no reference can leave this directory. Links are refused. A warning is written when Everyone, Users or Authenticated Users (Windows), or group or other (Linux, macOS), can read the file.

command.description: Schema 5.6.13. Settings of the command provider (command://<name>). Needed only when a reference uses it. The toolkit starts the executable directly with the argument list, with no shell, closes its standard input and reads its standard output as the secret (the trailing line break removed). A command that exits with a code other than 0 fails, and its standard error is reported without the secret.

executable.description: Schema 5.6.13. The program to start: a command name found on the path, or an absolute path. Not a command line: the arguments are in command.arguments.

arguments.description: Schema 5.6.13. The arguments, one list item each. The text {name} in an item is replaced by the name in the reference (command://<name>). At least one item must hold {name}. Each item is passed as one argument; nothing is split or quoted by a shell.

timeout_seconds.description: Schema 5.6.13. How long the command may run before it is stopped and the read fails. Default 30.

landing_zone.description: Part 2 of the implementation steps: the Azure foundation the instance depends on. Optional; leave it out when the foundation exists and is managed elsewhere.

subscriptions.description: Subscriptions by role. azure.subscription_id is the one the instance uses.

name.description: Name of the subscription; the other landing_zone entries refer to it.

id.description: Subscription id (a GUID). Use your own; the templates hold only a placeholder.

management_group.description: Management group the subscription is under.

resource_groups.description: Resource groups of the landing zone.

subscription.description: Name of a subscription in landing_zone.subscriptions.

location.description: Azure region of the resource group.

purpose.description: What the resource group is for, in words.

budgets.description: Cost Management budgets of the landing zone (schema 5.6.30; Microsoft Learn: Tutorial: Create and manage budgets). A budget is free: it tracks the cost of a subscription or a resource group and sends an e-mail when a threshold is passed; it never stops or deletes anything. Deploy-CostBudgets.ps1 and Deploy-CostBudgets.azcli.ps1 (phase 01, task 04) create each entry, and update an existing budget of the same name to what the file says. Leave the list out for no budget.

name.description: Name of the budget, unique in its scope: 1 to 63 letters, digits, hyphens and underscores (Microsoft Learn: Naming rules and restrictions, Microsoft.Consumption budgets).

scope.description: What the budget tracks: subscription (the whole subscription) or resource_group (one resource group of the subscription, named in resource_group).

subscription.description: Name of a subscription in landing_zone.subscriptions. Empty: azure.subscription_id.

resource_group.description: The resource group the budget tracks. Required when scope is resource_group, and not allowed otherwise. The resource group must exist (task 03).

amount.description: The amount of the budget for one time grain, in the billing currency of the subscription (a Cost Management budget carries no currency of its own). Greater than 0.

time_grain.description: The period the amount covers; the tracked cost starts again at 0 at the start of each period: Monthly, Quarterly or Annually (the BillingMonth, BillingQuarter and BillingAnnual grains of the API are for Web Direct accounts only and are not offered). Azure cannot change the time grain of an existing budget: the scripts report it and change nothing; delete the budget or use another name.

start_date.description: First day of the budget, YYYY-MM-01: the first of a month, on or after 2017-06-01 and not more than twelve months ahead (Microsoft Learn: Budgets - Create Or Update). Empty: the first day of the current month (UTC) when the budget is created; an existing budget keeps its start date.

end_date.description: Last day of the budget, YYYY-MM-DD, after start_date. Empty: Azure sets ten years after the start date; an existing budget keeps its end date.

thresholds.description: Percentages of the amount at which an e-mail is sent when the actual cost passes them, each greater than 0 and at most 1000. Together with forecast_thresholds at most five (a budget has at most five notifications). Default 80 and 100.

forecast_thresholds.description: Percentages of the amount at which an e-mail is sent when the forecast cost of the period passes them (an early warning), each greater than 0 and at most 1000. Empty: no forecast alert.

contact_emails.description: E-mail addresses that get the alert of every threshold. At least one.

subscription.description: Name of the subscription (landing_zone.subscriptions[].name) that holds the network.

address_space.description: Address ranges of the virtual network, in CIDR form.

dns_servers.description: DNS servers of the virtual network.

name.description: Name of the subnet, for example GatewaySubnet.

prefix.description: Address range of the subnet in CIDR form.

network_security_group.description: Name of the network security group on the subnet.

route_table.description: Name of the route table on the subnet.

allow_forwarded_traffic.description: Schema 5.6.23. Whether the peerings that start in this network accept traffic that was sent by a machine outside the peered network (Microsoft Learn: Virtual network peering, Allow forwarded traffic). Default true. A peering is made in both directions; each direction uses the options of the network it starts in.

allow_gateway_transit.description: Schema 5.6.23. Whether the peerings that start in this network let the peer use the VPN or ExpressRoute gateway of this network (Microsoft Learn: Virtual network peering, Gateway transit). Set it on the hub that has the gateway. Default false. Cannot be true together with use_remote_gateways on the same network.

use_remote_gateways.description: Schema 5.6.23. Whether the peerings that start in this network use the gateway of the peer (Microsoft Learn: Virtual network peering, Use remote gateways). Set it on the spokes. The peer must set allow_gateway_transit to true and have a gateway. Default false.

devops.description: Part 1 of the implementation steps: the pipeline platform, the project and its settings, the environments, the sign-in to Azure and the self-hosted runners (tasks 01 to 06 of automation / 01-cicd-infra). Optional. Schema 5.5 added repository, settings, environments, authentication, runners, runner_network, runner_access, api_token and state.key.

platform.description: The CI/CD platform: github, gitlab or azure_devops.

url.description: URL of the CI/CD platform (an organization or instance URL).

project.description: Name of the project or organization on the platform.

api_token.description: Schema 5.5. Key Vault reference to a token with administrator rights on the organization or project. The setup scripts (tasks 02 to 05) use it when the platform CLI is not already signed in. Without it they read GH_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN or AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT from the environment.

subscription.description: Schema 5.5. Name of the subscription in landing_zone.subscriptions that holds the runners (role devops). Default: the subscription with role devops.

resource_group.description: Schema 5.5. Resource group of the runners, their identity and their network.

create_resource_group.description: Schema 5.5. Create devops.resource_group. False when it exists.

repository.description: Schema 5.5. The deployment repository or project that task 02 creates.

template.description: GitHub: owner/repo of a template repository. GitLab: the ID or path of the template project. Azure DevOps: the clone URL to import. Empty creates an empty repository.

settings.description: Schema 5.5. What task 03 sets on the repository: branch protection, approvals and security.

required_approvals.description: Approvals a pull request needs before it merges. 0 for a sandbox.

reviewers.description: The team or group whose members review: a GitHub team slug (org/team), a GitLab group path or an Azure DevOps group name.

secret_scanning.description: Turn on secret scanning and push protection (GitHub), secret push rules (GitLab) or the secret file check (Azure DevOps).

resolve_conversations.description: All conversations must be resolved before a merge.

required_status_checks.description: Pipeline checks that must pass before a merge.

environments.description: Schema 5.5. The deployment environments that task 04 creates, with their approval gate.

name.description: Environment name, for example azr-prod-us, or ztp-reinstall for the approval in front of the ZTP Boot stage.

approval_required.description: A named reviewer must approve each deployment.

approvers.description: GitHub user names or org/team slugs, GitLab user names or group paths, Azure DevOps e-mail addresses.

deployment_branch.description: The only branch that may deploy to the environment.

pipelines.description: Schema 5.6.25. What the toolkit's own pipelines (the files under pipelines/) select: the runner label and the approval environment of each pipeline. Task 05 sets them as repository variables (GitHub) or project CI/CD variables (GitLab); Azure DevOps cannot read a variable there, so task 05 writes them into pipelines/azure-devops/variables/approval-environments.yml and pipeline-settings.yml, which the pipelines read when they are compiled (D126: no run parameter carries a deployment value). The pipeline files hold no runner label, pool or environment name of their own.

runner_label.description: Schema 5.6.25. The one label by which the pipelines choose the general runner: runs-on on GitHub (after self-hosted and linux) and tags on GitLab. It must be an entry of devops.runners[].labels of the general runner, and a label no other runner of the repository has. On GitLab the tags of a runner are set when its authentication token is created, so list the same tag in labels. Azure DevOps chooses the runner by its pool, devops.runners[].pool, and ignores this key.

environments.description: Schema 5.6.25. The approval environment of each pipeline. Each value is the name of an entry of devops.environments[] that has approval_required true; two pipelines may use the same entry.

os_configuration.description: Schema 5.6.25. The environment that gates the Apply job of the OS configuration pipelines (pipelines/github-actions/os-configuration.yml, pipelines/gitlab/os-configuration.gitlab-ci.yml, pipelines/azure-devops/os-configuration.yml).

os_configuration_clear_storage.description: Schema 5.6.25. The environment of the second approval in front of a storage wipe (stage ConfirmStorageWipe of pipelines/azure-devops/os-configuration.yml). Use other approvers than for os_configuration where you can.

arm_deployment.description: Schema 5.6.25. The environment that gates the Deploy job of the ARM deployment pipelines (pipelines/github-actions/arm-deployment.yml, pipelines/gitlab/stages/arm-deployment.yml, pipelines/azure-devops/arm-deployment.yml).

cicd_infra.description: Schema 5.6.25. The environment that gates the Apply job of the CI/CD infrastructure pipelines (the runners; pipelines/github-actions/cicd-infra.yml, pipelines/gitlab/stages/deploy-cicd-infra.yml, pipelines/azure-devops/cicd-infra.yml).

terraform_deployment.description: Schema 5.6.25. The environment that gates the Terraform apply and the on-premises Ansible jobs of the Terraform and Ansible sample pipelines (pipelines/github-actions/azure-local-deploy.yml, pipelines/azure-devops/azure-local-deploy.yml, pipelines/gitlab/.gitlab-ci.yml).

operations.description: Schema 5.6.28. The environment that gates every day 2 job that changes the cluster: the update (pipelines/github-actions/day2-update.yml, pipelines/gitlab/stages/day2-update.yml, pipelines/azure-devops/day2-update.yml), the node maintenance, the changing operations of the cluster operations pipeline, and the storage performance test of the validation pipeline. One environment for all of them on purpose: on Azure DevOps its Exclusive lock check then keeps an update and a node reboot from running on the cluster at the same time. Give it the approvers of your change process.

schedules.description: Schema 5.6.28. When the toolkit's scheduled pipelines run. A schedule is a five-field cron expression in UTC (the same syntax on GitHub Actions, GitLab CI and Azure DevOps; the platforms do not follow daylight saving time). GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps read a schedule only from the pipeline file (a cron expression cannot come from a variable there), so the sample pipeline file carries the default below and a test keeps the two equal; when you change the key, change the cron line of your copy of the pipeline file too. GitLab keeps a schedule in the project (CI/CD > Schedules), not in the file: create it with this value.

check_for_updates.description: Schema 5.6.28. When the day 2 check for updates runs (pipelines/github-actions/day2-check-updates.yml, pipelines/gitlab/stages/day2-check-updates.yml, pipelines/azure-devops/day2-check-updates.yml; owner directive D74: check for updates on a schedule). Five-field cron in UTC; empty means no schedule. The update agent of the cluster checks once a day (Learn: Use Azure Update Manager to update Azure Local), so daily is enough; the minute is not 0 because GitHub delays scheduled runs at the start of an hour, when many start at once. The run fails when the check finds something that needs attention (exit code 1), so the platform's own notification for a failed run is the alert. D126: the key works on all three platforms: task 05 writes it into the cron line of the GitHub workflow and of the Azure DevOps pipeline (with devops.repository.default_branch as the branch of the Azure DevOps schedule) and creates or updates the GitLab project schedule (deactivates it when the key is empty).

service_connection.description: Schema 5.6.27. Azure DevOps only. The name of the Azure Resource Manager service connection (workload identity federation) that task 05 creates and that the Azure DevOps pipelines sign in through; task 01 puts the same name in the subject of the federated credential. The pipelines (pipelines/azure-devops/*.yml) read it as AZL_SERVICE_CONNECTION, a compile-time variable of pipelines/azure-devops/variables/pipeline-settings.yml that task 05 writes (D126: not a run parameter). Required when devops.platform is azure_devops; GitHub and GitLab ignore it.

variable_group.description: Schema 5.6.27. Azure DevOps only. The name of the variable group (Pipelines > Library) task 05 writes the sign-in values (ARM_*) and the state settings (TF_BACKEND_*) to. With entries in devops.environments[] there is one group per environment, named <variable_group>-<environment>. The Azure DevOps pipelines that link a group (azure-local-deploy.yml, os-configuration.yml) read its name as AZL_VARIABLE_GROUP of pipelines/azure-devops/variables/pipeline-settings.yml, which task 05 writes with a group entry (D126: not a run parameter); task 05 also writes the group <name> for the repository, which the pipelines read. Required when devops.platform is azure_devops; GitHub and GitLab ignore it.

infrastructure_file.description: Schema 5.6.28. The path, in the deployment repository, of the infrastructure file the toolkit's pipelines pass to the scripts (-InfrastructureFile). Task 05 sets it as AZL_INFRASTRUCTURE_FILE (GitHub repository variable, GitLab project variable); the Azure DevOps pipelines read it as AZL_INFRASTRUCTURE_FILE of pipelines/azure-devops/variables/pipeline-settings.yml, which task 05 writes (D126: not a run parameter). The pipeline files hold no path of their own.

handoff_path.description: Schema 5.6.28. The repository path of the ZTP handoff files (a handoff file or a directory of *.ztp-handoff.json) the OS configuration pipelines pass to the script (-HandoffPath). A path that does not exist (a cluster installed from ISO) is not passed. Task 05 sets it as AZL_HANDOFF_PATH (GitHub, GitLab); the Azure DevOps pipeline reads it as AZL_HANDOFF_PATH of pipelines/azure-devops/variables/pipeline-settings.yml (none for no handoff), which task 05 writes (D126: not a run parameter). A run can instead take the artifact of a ZTP run (its run ID).

tool_versions.description: Schema 5.6.28. The tool versions every toolkit pipeline installs, the same on GitHub, GitLab and Azure DevOps. Task 05 sets each as an AZL_*_VERSION variable (GitHub repository variable, GitLab project variable, Azure DevOps variable group). The pipeline files hold no version of their own.

terraform.description: Schema 5.6.28. The Terraform release the pipelines install (AZL_TERRAFORM_VERSION): hashicorp/setup-terraform, TerraformInstaller, or pipelines/gitlab/Use-AzlGitLabTool.ps1. Default: the version the toolkit's runners carry (tool_versions.terraform of the cicd-runner module, cicd_runner_terraform_version of the Ansible role).

python.description: Schema 5.6.28. The Python minor version of the Ansible jobs (AZL_PYTHON_VERSION): actions/setup-python, UsePythonVersion, or the python<version> virtual environment of Use-AzlGitLabTool.ps1. ansible-core 2.21 needs 3.12 or later.

ansible_core.description: Schema 5.6.28. The ansible-core release the Ansible jobs install with pip (AZL_ANSIBLE_CORE_VERSION).

ansible_lint.description: Schema 5.6.28. The ansible-lint release the lint jobs install with pip (AZL_ANSIBLE_LINT_VERSION).

az_powershell.description: Schema 5.6.28. The Az PowerShell module version (AZL_AZ_POWERSHELL_VERSION): preferredAzurePowerShellVersion of AzurePowerShell@5 on Azure DevOps, Install-Module Az -RequiredVersion on GitHub and GitLab.

powershell_yaml.description: Schema 5.6.28. The powershell-yaml module version the pipelines install to read infrastructure.yml (AZL_POWERSHELL_YAML_VERSION). Default: the version the toolkit is tested with (README).

az_keyvault.description: Schema 5.6.28. The Az.KeyVault module version the pipelines install to read keyvault:// secrets (AZL_AZ_KEYVAULT_VERSION). Default: the version the toolkit is tested with (README).

authentication.description: Schema 5.5. How the pipelines sign in to Azure (tasks 01 and 05). The app registration is azure.automation_identity.name.

method.description: oidc: a federated credential per repository and environment, no secret. client_secret: a secret, stored only in Key Vault (devops.authentication.client_secret) and in the platform as a masked variable. Every toolkit pipeline follows it: task 05 sets AZL_AUTH_METHOD (GitHub, GitLab, the Azure DevOps variable group), and the sign-in steps choose OIDC or the secret by it (schema 5.6.28). A managed identity of the runner is not a method of the pipelines.

client_secret.description: Key Vault reference where task 01 stores the generated client secret (method client_secret).

roles.description: Roles the service principal gets on each subscription. Default: Contributor and User Access Administrator, as the automation docs say. Narrow them when you can.

grant_graph_role_management.description: Also add the Microsoft Graph application permission RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory and grant admin consent. High privilege: leave false unless a pipeline assigns Entra roles.

register_encryption_at_host.description: Register Microsoft.Compute and the EncryptionAtHost feature on each subscription.

runners.description: Schema 5.5. The self-hosted runners that task 06 deploys with Terraform. One Linux general pool and at most one Windows ztp runner; use the module directly for more. Replaces devops.runner when present.

name.description: Name prefix of the VM or VMs, for example vm-contoso-runner-lnx.

purpose.description: general: ARM, Arc, Terraform, Ansible and OS configuration. ztp: the azurelocal-ztp Boot, Bootstrap and Vouchers stages (Windows only).

compute_type.description: vm or vmss. Windows and ztp runners are VMs.

size.description: VM size. Default Standard_D2s_v5 (Linux) and Standard_D4s_v5 (Windows ztp).

labels.description: Labels added to the defaults (azure, the OS, terraform, ansible, ztp). The pipelines choose the general runner by one of them, devops.pipelines.runner_label.

registration_secret.description: Key Vault reference to the secret the runner reads at boot: a PAT or App token (GitHub), the runner authentication token (GitLab), a PAT with Agent Pools read and manage (Azure DevOps). Only the reference is here.

pool.description: The Azure Pipelines agent pool, or the GitHub runner group. A ztp runner gets its own. Required on Azure DevOps (task 06 stops without it, there is no default pool); the Azure DevOps pipelines read the pool of the general runner as AZL_AGENT_POOL of pipelines/azure-devops/variables/pipeline-settings.yml, which task 05 writes (D126).

private_ips.description: Static private addresses, one per VM. Empty uses dynamic addresses.

name.description: Name of the subnet the runner machines are placed in.

prefix.description: Address range of that subnet, in CIDR form.

data_disk_gb.description: Data disk for the ZTP media, images and vouchers. 512 or more for ztp.

admin_ssh_public_key.description: Schema 5.6.28. The SSH public key of the administrator of a Linux runner (a public key, not a secret): the key itself (ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa or ecdsa-sha2-nistp*), or a reference the toolkit's secret resolver reads (file://<name> in secrets.file.directory, keyvault://, env://, command://). Task 05 sets AZL_RUNNER_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY from the general Linux runner's key (GitHub, GitLab, the Azure DevOps variable group), and task 06 reads it from there.

admin_username.description: Schema 5.6.28. Local administrator user name of the runner machines: the admin_username Terraform gives the VMs, and the account the Ansible cicd_runner playbook connects as (ansible_user of the cicd-runners inventory).

identity_client_id.description: Schema 5.6.28. Client (application) ID of the runner's user-assigned managed identity (GUID), once it exists. Not a secret.

nsg_name.description: Schema 5.6.28. Name of the network security group of the runner subnet. Task 06 needs it; set an existing group's name to adopt it with terraform import.

managed_identity_name.description: Schema 5.6.28. Name of the user-assigned managed identity the runner signs in to Azure as. Task 06 needs it.

windows_admin_password_secret.description: Schema 5.6.28. Windows runners only: Key Vault reference to the secret task 06 writes the generated administrator password to. The vault must be the vault of registration_secret. Absent: the password is kept in the Terraform state only.

zones.description: Schema 5.6.28. Availability zones the runner machines are spread over (the VM scale set spans them). Empty: no zone.

os_disk_size_gb.description: Schema 5.6.28. Size of the OS disk in GB. Absent: the size the Terraform module gives the OS (default_os_disk_size_gb: 64 on Linux, 128 on Windows).

os_disk_type.description: Schema 5.6.28. Storage type of the OS disk and of the data disk. Default Premium_LRS.

os_disk_caching.description: Schema 5.6.28. Caching of the OS disk. Default ReadWrite.

data_disk_caching.description: Schema 5.6.28. Caching of the data disk (data_disk_gb). Default ReadWrite.

encryption_at_host.description: Schema 5.6.28. Encryption at host of the runner machines. The Microsoft.Compute/EncryptionAtHost feature must be registered on the subscription (task 01 does this with devops.authentication.register_encryption_at_host). Default false.

image.description: Schema 5.6.28. Marketplace image of the runner machines. Absent: the image the Terraform module gives the OS (default_images: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on Linux, Windows Server 2025 Datacenter Azure Edition on Windows).

runner_network.description: Schema 5.5. The VNet of the runners, the peering with the hub and the lab ranges they reach.

vnet_name.description: Name of the virtual network the runners are placed in.

address_space.description: Address ranges of that virtual network, in CIDR form.

dns_servers.description: DNS servers of that virtual network.

hub_peering.description: Peering with the hub VNet. The hub half is created in the hub subscription unless create_hub_side is false.

enabled.description: Peer the runner VNet with the hub.

hub_network.description: Name of the hub in landing_zone.networks (its subscription and resource group give the VNet ID).

hub_vnet_id.description: Resource ID of the hub VNet. Use it instead of hub_network.

use_remote_gateways.description: Use the hub VPN or ExpressRoute gateway to reach the lab.

create_hub_side.description: Create the hub half of the peering. False when the network team owns it.

spoke_name.description: Schema 5.6.28. Name of the spoke half of the peering (on the runner VNet). Needed when enabled is true.

hub_name.description: Schema 5.6.28. Name of the hub half of the peering (on the hub VNet). Needed when enabled and create_hub_side are true.

reachable_cidrs.description: Lab networks the runners reach: management, storage, BMC.

reachable_tcp_ports.description: TCP ports allowed outbound to the lab networks. Default 22, 443, 445, 3389, 5985, 5986.

bmc_cidrs.description: The BMC networks. The ztp runner accepts inbound TCP 445 from these only. Required for a ztp runner.

admin_source_cidrs.description: Ranges that may reach SSH or RDP on the runners. Empty allows none.

allow_internet_https.description: Schema 5.6.28. The runner NSG allows HTTPS (443) outbound to the internet: GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, package repositories and runner downloads. Default true.

allow_internet_http.description: Schema 5.6.28. The runner NSG allows HTTP (80) outbound to the internet: package mirrors with signed metadata. Default true.

allow_icmp.description: Schema 5.6.28. The runner NSG allows ICMP outbound to reachable_cidrs and bmc_cidrs, for reachability checks. Default true.

runner_access.description: Schema 5.5. What the runners may do in Azure (least privilege).

resource_groups.description: Resource groups where the runners are Contributor. Default: azure.resource_group. Add the Azure Local managed resource group if it can take deployments.

rbac_administrator.description: Role Based Access Control Administrator on those resource groups, which the Azure Local deployment and ZTP need.

rbac_delegable_role_ids.description: Limit the roles the runners may assign to these role definition GUIDs. Empty allows any role.

arc_run_command.description: Azure Connected Machine Resource Administrator on those resource groups, so jobs can run Arc Run Command on the machines.

key_vaults.description: Vaults the runners read secrets from. Default: every vault in key_vaults.

additional_role_assignments.description: Schema 5.6.28. Other role assignments of the runner identities, each with a short name, a scope (a resource ID) and a role name.

name.description: Short name of the assignment (unique in the list).

scope.description: Resource ID of the scope: a subscription, a resource group or a resource.

role_definition_name.description: Name of the role, for example Reader.

runner.description: One runner (the form before devops.runners[]). Kept for files written before 5.5; use devops.runners[].

type.description: Kind of runner: vm, container_app or existing.

labels.description: Runner tags or labels that jobs select.

registration_token.description: A Key Vault secret reference: keyvault://<vault>/<secret>. The vault must be listed in key_vaults.

state.description: Where the Terraform state is kept.

subscription_id.description: Schema 5.5. Subscription of the state storage account.

key.description: Schema 5.5. Blob name of the CI/CD runners state. Default cicd-infra.tfstate.

storage_account.description: Storage account that holds the state.

container.description: Blob container that holds the state. Default tfstate (task 05 sets TF_BACKEND_CONTAINER for the pipelines, task 06 and New-IacVariableFiles.ps1 write it to the backend settings).

resource_group.description: Resource group of the state storage account.

azure_local_key.description: Schema 5.6.28. Blob name of the state of the azure-local Terraform environment (src/terraform/environments/azure-local). Default azure-local.tfstate. Task 05 sets TF_BACKEND_KEY from it for the pipelines, and the generated backend.hcl names it.

netbios_name.description: Up to 15 letters, digits and hyphens.

kv_ref.description: A secret reference, never a secret value. Four forms, one per provider: keyvault://<vault>/<secret> (the vault must be listed in key_vaults), env://<VARIABLE_NAME>, file://<name> (a file in secrets.file.directory) and command://<name> (the command in secrets.command). The format keeps its old name, kv_ref. See docs/secret-references.md. (the three non-Key-Vault forms since 5.6.13)

username.description: A reference to the secret holding the user name, or the user name itself.

rfs_write_attribute.description: Schema 5.4. azurelocal-ztp, Boot stage: also set the iDRAC Remote File Share attribute RFS.<n>.WriteProtected to Read Write before it inserts the virtual media. iDRAC 7.30 rejects WriteProtected=false in InsertMedia, and the maintenance environment cannot write its voucher to a read-only drive. Default: true for Dell (azurelocal-ztp config/oem/dell.json, bmc.rfsWriteAttribute), false for the other vendors, whose BMCs have no such attribute. Set it when your BMC differs from its vendor's usual behaviour.

verify_certificate.description: Schema 5.4. Check the BMCs' TLS certificates. Default false: BMCs ship a self-signed certificate, so azurelocal-ztp accepts it. Set true once the BMCs carry a certificate that the management host trusts.

node.description: One machine. Describe its management port either with management (schema 5.0) or, from 5.2, with network_adapters, which lists every port and derives management from the port that owns the management address.

name.description: Host name: up to 15 characters. Also the edge machine name and, for an ISO install, the Arc machine name. With simplified provisioning the Arc machine name is arc_machine_name, which defaults to this.

management.description: The machine's management port and address (schema 5.0 and 5.1). From 5.2, network_adapters describes it instead: the port with role management and an ip_assignment other than none. When both are given they must agree; prefer network_adapters.

ip_address.description: Management address. ARM physicalNodesSettings[].ipv4Address. How it gets onto the management port before deployment is networking.management.ip_assignment: set on the port (static), reserved in DHCP for mac_address (dhcp), or already there (preconfigured). With network_adapters it is the management port's ip_address.

mac_address.description: MAC of the management port. Provisioning finds and targets the port by it: simplified provisioning names the port by this MAC when it sets the static address (edge machine networkAdapters[].macAddress), and node preparation finds the adapter by it. With ip_assignment dhcp, reserve ip_address for this MAC. Required with simplified provisioning.

adapter_name.description: Name of the management port in the installed OS, for example 'SLOT 3 Port 1'. Optional: mac_address identifies the port. Simplified provisioning also sends it with the port's settings; leave it out unless you know the name the OS gives the port.

network_adapters.description: Every physical network port of the machine (schema 5.2): name, MAC, roles and how each gets its host address. Exactly one port owns the management address: role management and an ip_assignment other than none. Intents name ports by these names. List them on every node or on none.

serial_number.description: Serial number (Dell service tag). Maps each simplified-provisioning voucher to its machine.

zone.description: Rack-aware: the local availability zone. ARM localAvailabilityZones.

storage_ips.description: Storage address on each storage network, in networking.storage.networks order, when networking.storage.auto_ip is false.

arc_machine_name.description: Name of the machine's Arc resource (Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines). Default: name. Simplified provisioning sets it when it claims the machine (edge machine arcMachineResourceId); without it the service names the Arc machine ROE1-<id>, and an Arc machine can't be renamed. The deployment uses it in ARM arcNodeResourceIds. An ISO install registers the Arc machine under the host name, so leave it out there. 1-54 letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', not ending in '.'.

arc_resource_name.description: Deprecated: use arc_machine_name. Read as arc_machine_name when that isn't set.

bios.description: BIOS attributes for this machine in their FINAL state, merged over hardware.bios (a key here wins). See hardware.bios.

bios_during_provisioning.description: Schema 5.3. Temporary BIOS attributes for this machine's OS install only, merged over hardware.bios_during_provisioning (a key here wins); during-provisioning values win over bios. azurelocal-ztp sets each key back to its bios value in its Restore stage. See hardware.bios_during_provisioning.

maintenance_address.description: Schema 5.3. Simplified provisioning: the address the machine's maintenance environment answers on (its Configurator service, TCP 20001), when it is known: a DHCP reservation, or an address set at the console. azurelocal-ztp's Device stage then talks to it directly. Without it, the Device stage finds the maintenance environment by MAC, scanning networking.management.provisioning_dhcp_range.

san.description: Schema 5.3. This machine's SAN connections: its Fibre Channel HBAs and their WWPNs (storage.san.type fibre_channel), or its iSCSI initiator IQN (storage.san.type iscsi; the iSCSI ports' addresses are on network_adapters with role iscsi:a and iscsi:b). Needed on every machine when storage.san.type is set.

adapters.description: Adapters of the intent, by the key nodes[].network_adapters[].name (the port's name in this file, the same on every machine; the file finds the physical adapter by its MAC, so the OS may call it anything). With nodes[].network_adapters (5.2) each name must be a port in every node's list. The name the deployment sends to Azure (ARM intentList adapter) is what the OS calls that adapter on the nodes, found by MAC, or nodes[].network_adapters[].os_name_override when the file sets one. The first adapter matters: the management virtual adapter takes the MAC of the first adapter of the management intent, so that adapter owns the management address.

overrides.description: Network ATC overrides. Leave out to keep Network ATC's defaults, which Microsoft recommends.

purpose.description: What the network is for (since 5.6). management and oob mark a network the machines' remote management may be reached from: the remote management security profile adds its subnet to the allowed sources of dev and production (a candidate, not a trust: prefer listing the controller addresses in os_configuration.remoting.allowed_source_cidrs). automation, compute, storage and other have no effect on remote management.

bios_settings.description: BIOS attributes: vendor attribute name -> value, as the BMC's Redfish Bios resource names them (Attributes of /redfish/v1/Systems/<id>/Bios). Values are strings, even for numbers; tools convert them to the type the BMC reports. azurelocal-ztp applies them in its Boot stage, before the maintenance boot: it reads the current values, PATCHes only those that differ to the Bios Settings resource with @Redfish.SettingsApplyTime OnReset, powers the machine on or restarts it, and waits until the BIOS reports every value. Used twice: as bios (the machine's FINAL state) and as bios_during_provisioning (TEMPORARY values for the OS install, which the Restore stage sets back to the bios values). Dell examples: Slot2: Disabled (turn off the card in PCIe slot 2, for example a Fibre Channel HBA whose SAN LUN the maintenance environment would otherwise install onto; as a temporary value, with Slot2: Enabled in bios); Slot2: BootDriverDisabled (the card stays visible to the OS but never boots); EmbNic1Nic2: Enabled (the embedded LOM ports, when they show as DisabledOs and the OS can't see them).

additionalProperties.description: The value of the BIOS attribute, as a string.

wwpn.description: A Fibre Channel World Wide Port Name: 16 hexadecimal digits, as 8 colon-separated pairs (50:00:09:72:08:12:34:56) or without colons.

iscsi_name.description: An iSCSI qualified name (iqn.yyyy-mm.reversed.domain[:identifier]), or an eui. or naa. name.

iscsi_portal.description: An iSCSI target portal: an IPv4 address, optionally with :port (default 3260).

node_san.description: One machine's SAN connections (schema 5.3). Fibre Channel: hbas, each with its slot and ports, and every port's WWPN and fabric. iSCSI: initiator_iqn.

hbas.description: The host bus adapters in this machine that reach the SAN: Fibre Channel HBAs, and from 5.4 iSCSI offload adapters. azurelocal-ztp reads their slots (schema 5.4): while the OS installs it turns those PCIe slots off in the BIOS, so the maintenance environment can't install onto a SAN LUN, and turns them on again afterwards (provisioning.simplified.isolate_san_adapters).

slot.description: Where the HBA is, as a PCIe slot label: Slot 2, Slot2 or slot-2 (the number is what counts). azurelocal-ztp turns the BIOS attribute of that slot off for the OS install and puts it back afterwards; the attribute name per vendor is in its config/oem/<vendor>.json. For another label (for example OCP 1), or a vendor azurelocal-ztp has no mapping for, give bios_attribute.

type.description: Schema 5.4. fibre_channel (default; with storage.san.type fibre_channel the ports with their WWPNs are needed for zoning, rule AZL-028) or iscsi_offload (an adapter that presents SAN LUNs to the BIOS; it needs no ports here, its addresses are on network_adapters with role iscsi:a or iscsi:b).

bios_attribute.description: Schema 5.4. The vendor's BIOS attribute name for this adapter's slot, as the BMC's Redfish Bios resource names it. With no vendor mapping in azurelocal-ztp this is the only way to isolate the adapter during the install; with a mapping it overrides the attribute derived from slot. An explicit bios_during_provisioning key for the same attribute still wins.

bios_disabled_value.description: Schema 5.4. The value of bios_attribute that turns the slot off for the OS install. Default: the vendor mapping's disabled value, else Disabled.

bios_enabled_value.description: Schema 5.4. The value that turns the slot back on when azurelocal-ztp finds it already at bios_disabled_value in the Restore stage (for example a crashed earlier run left it off). Otherwise Restore puts back the value it found before the install. Default: the vendor mapping's enabled value, else Enabled.

initiator_iqn.description: The machine's iSCSI initiator name. Unique in the file.

network_adapter.description: One physical network port of the machine (schema 5.2). List every port, used or not, so each tool reads the same NICs. A port can carry several roles (a converged design).

name.description: The port's name in this file: the key that networking.intents[].adapters, networking.storage.networks[].adapter and networking.cluster_networks[].adapter use. The same on every machine, unique on the machine. It labels a physical adapter that is found on the node by mac_address, so it does not have to be the name the OS gave the adapter (OS names differ between installs and between ZTP and ISO installs, for example Port0, SLOT 3 Port 1 or NIC1). Discovery writes it from the slot and the port, for example 'Slot 3 Port 1'. The name the deployment sends to Azure is what the OS calls the adapter (read by MAC) or os_name_override when set. A file that already uses the OS name here keeps working.

mac_address.description: The port's identity. Tools find the physical adapter on a node by this MAC (case and separators are ignored), never by a name: node preparation, the ARM parameters and the pre-cluster verification all resolve the OS adapter name from it. Hardware discovery writes it. Required. Also needed for a DHCP reservation and, with simplified provisioning, for the management port.

slot.description: Where the port is, for example Embedded (a LOM), Slot 3 or OCP 1. From 5.4 azurelocal-ztp reads it: a management or provisioning port in slot Embedded makes it enable the embedded NICs in the BIOS (provisioning.simplified.enable_embedded_nics), and a slot that also holds a SAN adapter (nodes[].san.hbas[].slot) is never turned off.

port_index.description: The number of the port on its adapter, counted from 1, as the BMC reports it (Redfish PhysicalPortNumber, else the order of the port on the card). With slot and pci_location it says which physical connector the port is. Written by hardware discovery; a record of the hardware, nothing is configured from it.

pci_location.description: Where the adapter sits on the PCI bus, as hardware discovery reports it (bus, device, function as decimal numbers). A verification aid, informational: OS configuration compares it with the node's own hardware information (Get-NetAdapterHardwareInfo) and reports a difference; the port is still found by mac_address.

vendor.description: The adapter manufacturer as hardware discovery reports it, for example the Manufacturer of the Redfish NetworkAdapter. Informational: no tool behaves differently for a brand; every make is handled through the same keys (mac_address, slot, port_index, model, speed_gbps, rdma).

os_name_override.description: Optional, off by default. The name you want this adapter to have in the OS, for example 'Mgmt1', 'Compute1' or 'Storage1'. Without it nothing is renamed: the OS configuration step NicNames leaves every adapter name alone and the deployment sends the name the OS already uses (found by mac_address). With it, NicNames renames the adapter found by mac_address to this name (a guarded change, idempotent, the management adapter last) and the deployment sends this name. Give the same value for the same port (name) on every machine: Network ATC needs one adapter name per intent adapter on every node. 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, space, underscore, dot, hyphen and parentheses.

model.description: Card model, for example 'NVIDIA ConnectX-6 Dx'. Ports in one intent must be the same make, model and speed.

roles.description: What the port is for: management, compute, storage (the Network ATC traffic types), provisioning (the maintenance environment of simplified provisioning reaches Azure through this port, before the machine is claimed; how it gets its address there is networking.management.provisioning_network), iscsi:a or iscsi:b (schema 5.3: a port that carries iSCSI traffic to the SAN's fabric A or B; give it a static address, prefix_length and VLAN, no gateway), or unused. A converged port lists several, for example [management, compute]. unused stands alone.

ip_assignment.description: How the installed OS gets this port's host address before deployment. For the management port this is the management address mode (config/variables/docs/infrastructure-file.md): dhcp_reservation is Mode A (Reserved, recommended); static is Mode B (Static with DHCP) or Mode C (Static without management DHCP). static: ip_address is set on the port (with simplified provisioning azurelocal-ztp's Device stage sets it by MAC before the OS install, the install resets every port to DHCP, and OS configuration sets it again by MAC; otherwise the operator or the toolkit). dhcp_reservation: the port keeps DHCP and the DHCP server reserves ip_address for mac_address. dhcp: the port keeps DHCP with no reservation, so its address can change (a warning). preconfigured: the port is already configured; tools leave it alone. none: no host address before deployment (Network ATC or the storage networks give it one, or it isn't used); node preparation turns DHCP off on it. Exactly one management port per machine owns the management address: the one with role management and an ip_assignment other than none.

ip_address.description: The host address. For the management port this is ARM physicalNodesSettings[].ipv4Address. Required with static. With dhcp_reservation give the reserved address: without it the tools can only check that the port has a DHCP address (a warning), and the deployment still needs it unless use_dhcp is true (a file with scope ztp doesn't deploy).

prefix_length.description: Prefix length of ip_address. Default for the management port: from networking.management.subnet, which it must match.

gateway.description: Default gateway on this port. Default for the management port: networking.management.gateway. Leave it out on every other port: validation fails when more than one physical adapter has a default gateway.

dns_servers.description: Default for the management port: networking.management.dns_servers, which it must match.

vlan_id.description: The VLAN of this port's traffic. With vlan_mode tagged the host tags it; with vlan_mode access the switch port is an access port in this VLAN and the host sends untagged frames (it records the switch side). Without vlan_mode, 0 or absent means untagged and anything else is tagged by the host.

vlan_mode.description: access: the switch port is an access (untagged) port; the host doesn't tag, so simplified provisioning sends VLAN 0. tagged: the switch port is a trunk and the host tags vlan_id.

allowed_vlans.description: Optional. The VLAN ids the switch port of this adapter allows, when the port is a trunk that carries more than the VLAN of the port itself: the tenant (compute) VLANs of the compute adapters. The pre-cluster verification checks that every VLAN used by compute traffic in networking.vlans[] and networking.logical_networks[] is in this list on the compute adapters; without it a tagged compute port is reported Skipped (the file says nothing about what the port allows). This is switch-side metadata for the checklist of the gate; it does not configure the switch or the NIC.

switch.description: The switch, for example a network_devices[].hostname.

port.description: The switch port, for example Ethernet1/11.
